scopeData.label: Data
scopeData.value: Official vendor spec pages are the primary source; verifiable gaps are filled by manual review

about.why: Why this shape: phones get a few launches a year and the data changes slowly, so a static snapshot plus git history is enough — the front end needs no secrets and no runtime dependencies. Buckets use percentiles of the current on-sale pool rather than absolute thresholds, so they will not silently expire in three years. Copy is generated from data by templates, never by an LLM, so claims like "this is the brightest-screen phone" stay reproducible and traceable.

principleOne.title: Sources: official specs + manual review
principleOne.body: The primary source is each vendor's official spec page. Fields the vendor does not publish but that can be verified against an independently checkable source (regulatory network-access approval, teardown report, official manual) are filled in by manual review and recorded in the user data layer. All data is labelled as a whole as "from vendor sites and manual review" rather than tagged field by field.

principleTwo.title: Gaps are labelled "not published"
principleTwo.body: Fields that can neither be obtained from the vendor site nor verified against a reliable independent source are recorded as missing and shown as "not published" — never estimated, never inferred from the model name. Rankings use only the extremes of genuinely comparable fields and never third-party benchmark scores.

principleThree.title: Data integrity is a hard rule
principleThree.body: Every label must have a source. Form judgments such as "foldable" require verbatim evidence from the vendor site; attributes the source does not state — screen curvature, for example — are never invented. Manually added fields must likewise cite their source and reason.

principleFour.title: The test is a content fingerprint, not a git diff
principleFour.body: The data carries a set of runtime fields that change on every run. Those fields are stripped before the fingerprint is computed, so a commit and publish only happen when the data or template actually changed — instead of manufacturing an empty commit every 12 hours.

principleFive.title: Automated gates stand before every write
principleFive.body: Parsers, validation gates and geometry pure functions are all covered by self-tests (196 of them), enforced by the first CI job. The gates are themselves reverse-tested: injecting a violation must turn them red and reverting must restore green — otherwise a green light means nothing.

licenseCode.name: Code & scripts
licenseCode.body: Site code, data pipeline, validation gates and self-tests are all open source.

licenseData.name: Device data
licenseData.body: Specs come primarily from each vendor's official spec page (factual data belonging to each vendor; this site claims no additional licence). Fields the vendor does not publish but that can be verified against independent sources such as regulatory approvals, teardown reports or official manuals are filled in by manual review. Gaps that cannot be verified are marked "not published" and never inferred.

licenseTrademark.name: Model names & trademarks
licenseTrademark.body: Model names and trademarks on these pages belong to their respective owners and are used here only to identify the products being described; they imply no affiliation or endorsement.

about.artNote: This site relies on no custom art assets — the entire visual layer is built from a system font stack and component library.

search.title: Search models
search.placeholder: Model / Chinese name / product line / chip, e.g. mate, Pura, nova, Kirin
search.looseHint: Matched ignoring case and spaces — what you typed "{q}" may officially be written "{name}"
search.tipA: Separate words with spaces; all of them must match. Searchable: model name, Chinese name, product line, chip.
search.tipBold: Case, spaces, full- and half-width are all ignored
search.noResultBody: Fields the vendor does not publish are not indexed. Include the key part of the model name (e.g. "Mate 60 Pro", or write "mate60pro").

timeline.title: Release timeline
timeline.note: Dates come from official vendor releases; when precision is insufficient they are shown by year or month.
timeline.lifecycleNote: Each machine's lifecycle by product line: release → on sale → retired. Unknown retirement dates get a dashed tail (no estimation); inverted timelines surface here.
timeline.invertedDetail: Release {start} is later than retirement {retired} — data needs verification
timeline.onlyInvertedHint: Inverted = retirement earlier than release; a data incident that needs manual verification
